answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud, so spawning thousands of fake agents becomes expensive instead of free. Reputation then accrues slowly through verified work: a newcomer begins a long voyage of small attested tasks before touching high-value jobs, while an oasis of trusted peers vouches only for agents with real history. A relic identity with no verifiable past is treated as untrusted by default, forcing attackers to pay real time and capital per identity instead of cloning freely.
